text: # Eiffel Tower The Eiffel Tower is a wrought-iron lattice tower on the Champ de Mars in Paris, France. It is named after Gustave Eiffel, whose company designed and built the tower. The tower was constructed from 1887 to 1889 as the centerpiece of the 1889 Exposition Universelle, a world's fair held to celebrate the 100th anniversary of the French Revolution. Many prominent French artists and intellectuals initially criticized its design. When it was completed, the tower was the tallest man-made structure in the world, a title it held until the Chrysler Building in New York City was finished in 1930. Its height is about 330 metres including antennas. The tower has three levels open to visitors, with restaurants on the first and second levels.

# Python (programming language) Python is a high-level, general-purpose programming language created by Guido van Rossum. Van Rossum began working on Python in the late 1980s as a successor to the ABC language, and the first version, Python 0.9.0, was released in February 1991. The language is named after the British comedy group Monty Python, not after the snake. Python's design philosophy emphasizes code readability, and it uses significant indentation to delimit blocks of code. Python 2.0 was released in October 2000 and introduced features such as list comprehensions and a cycle-detecting garbage collector. Python 3.0 was released in December 2008. It was a major revision that was not completely backward-compatible with earlier versions. Python 2 reached its end of life on January 1, 2020, after which it no longer received security patches. Van Rossum served as the project's "Benevolent Dictator For Life" until he stepped down from the role in July 2018. Python is now governed by a five-member steering council elected by the core developers.
